title: Turmeric farming offers hope of reviving local employment in Nepal village - The Climate Watch
description: Turmeric farming offers hope of reviving local employment in Nepal village  The Climate Watch
publisher.title: The Climate Watch
full_article:
A community-led agroforestry initiative in Dhanusha is expanding income opportunities through turmeric cultivation, supported by FAO, while creating seasonal jobs and offering an alternative to overseas labour migration.

With their husbands working abroad, many women in Pushpalpur, Ward No. 4 of Mithila Municipality in Dhanusha district, Nepal, shoulder the responsibility of supporting their families on their own. While overseas employment has long been a necessity to sustain household incomes, these women are now beginning to see opportunities for earning a living within their own village. Turmeric cultivation, launched in the Bhatighari Community Forest, has become more than just an agricultural venture; it has given them renewed hope of reuniting their families by creating employment at home.

Meena Tamang, a resident of Pushpalpur, Ward No. 4, Mithila Municipality, says her husband is currently working overseas. Living apart from her family was never her choice but a necessity.

“My husband had to go abroad to support our family,” she says. “If we had a steady source of income here, I would want him to stay and work in the village instead.”

Most households in Pushpalpur have at least one male family member employed overseas. Buddhamaya Moktan, another resident of the village, also has a husband working abroad. Living with her two sons and one daughter, she dreams of having her family together again. For families forced to live apart due to the lack of local employment, the nearby Bhatighari Community Forest has become a source of hope.

The women believe that turmeric cultivation in the community forest will create employment opportunities in the coming years, allowing their husbands to return from overseas and find work in their own village. This year alone, they planted 5,400 kilograms of turmeric seed rhizomes in the community forest. According to Shyam Gole, chairperson of the Community Forest User Group, one quintal of turmeric seed can produce five to seven quintals of fresh turmeric. Based on this estimate, the group expects the 5,400 kg planted this year to yield approximately 32,400 kg of turmeric.

According to Meena Tamang, secretary of the Community Forest User Group, local people will be employed in activities such as cultivation, processing, packaging and marketing of turmeric.

“We plan to package and market the turmeric ourselves. Once that happens, many more people in the village will have employment opportunities,” she says.

In the Nepali market, ground turmeric powder currently sells for NPR 300 to NPR 600 per kilogram. Local initiatives have been supported by the Forest and Agriculture Facilitation Programme, implemented with assistance from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Through the programme, the community has received turmeric seed, agricultural tools for land preparation and support for the construction of a turmeric processing centre.

A model community forest

Located about one kilometre from the East-West Mahendra Highway, the Bhatighari Community Forest has been successfully protected and managed through the active participation of residents. It has also emerged as an exemplary model of agroforestry.

The forest is home to more than 500 mango trees. Every year, once the trees begin flowering, the Community Forest User Group sells the standing mango crop to traders through advance contracts worth NPR 1 million to NPR 1.5 million.

Beyond generating income from mango production, the forest also creates employment for local people. Villagers are hired to clear undergrowth, maintain the forest and cultivate turmeric. Around 40 households receive employment for approximately 30 days each year, earning NPR 700 per day, providing an important source of seasonal income for the community.

title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh pass, calls it unjustified - News On AIR
description: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh pass, calls it unjustified  News On AIR
publisher.title: News On AIR
full_article:
India has rejected Nepal’s claim over Lipulekh Pass, termed it as a long-standing route for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra since 1954 and the Yatra through this route has been going on for decades. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in a social media post said this in response to claims related to border issues made by Foreign Ministry of Nepal in the context of the annual Kailash Manasarovar Yatra.

He stressed that India’s position in this regard had been consistent and clear and this is not a new development. Mr Jaiswal pointed out that India has consistently maintained that such claims are neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. He stressed that such unilateral artificial enlargement of territorial claims is untenable. The spokesperson added that India remains open to a constructive interaction with Nepal on all issues in the bilateral relationship, including on resolving agreed outstanding boundary issues through dialogue and diplomacy.

title: Nepal Quality Council approves new quality standards to align with international practices - Khabarhub
description: Nepal Quality Council approves new quality standards to align with international practices  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: The 11th meeting of the Nepal Quality Council has approved draft Nepal Quality and International Standards aimed at improving quality regulation and aligning domestic practices with global standards.

The meeting endorsed various quality standards recommended by the technical committee formed for the determination and review of quality standards in Nepal.

Representatives from concerned ministries and officials from relevant organisations participated in the meeting.

The council approved specifications for ethanol used as a blending component in motor gasoline and standards related to elastomeric bridge bearings.

It also endorsed several international standards related to rubber hardness testing, along with standards for determining the compression set of rubber and thermoplastics.

According to the council, the decision was taken to update Nepal’s quality standards in line with current requirements and international practices.

The newly approved standards are expected to enhance quality in industrial and production sectors, strengthen testing systems and help Nepali products meet international benchmarks.

The council said the process of quality determination and review would also become more systematic and effective following the implementation of the updated standards.

title: Nepal brought back its tigers. Now, it has to figure out how to live with them. - The World from PRX
description: Nepal brought back its tigers. Now, it has to figure out how to live with them.  The World from PRX
publisher.title: The World from PRX
full_article:
Twenty years ago, Birendra Mahato founded the Tharu Cultural Museum near Chitwan National Park — Nepal’s first national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — to preserve an Indigenous way of life he feared was fading.

Inside, displays of practices of the Tharu people, who are native to Nepal’s southern plains, sit alongside reminders of when the nation’s forests were a hunting ground for the country’s elite.

“These are sometimes very painful stories,” Mahato said, pointing to a photo of a former prime minister of Nepal in front of 300 tiger skins — nearly as many as the whole population recorded in the last tiger census.

He said outsiders had nearly hunted a species of tiger to extinction that the Tharu had long lived alongside.

“Even some years we lost our relatives, our ancestors from the tigers, but we didn’t mind because our ancestors thought: “We live in the same area, same region. Sometimes tigers [are] harmful for us, sometimes we are harmful to the tiger,” he said.

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.34.33-PM-1024x670.png Birendra Mahato stands outside the Tharu Cultural Museum near Nepal’s Chitwan National Park. Danielle Preiss/The World

Hunting and habitat loss had decimated tiger populations in Nepal and around the world. But after decades of decline, Nepal began one of the world’s most successful tiger recoveries. In 2010, Nepal joined 12 other countries pledging to double their numbers by 2022 — Nepal nearly tripled them instead. But now, locals are struggling to coexist with the predators.

As tiger numbers have increased, so have concerns about deadly encounters with people. Panta says the solution is to keep tigers in protected areas while creating livelihoods for people outside them.

“We are trying to support the local community in that way so that they do not require [entering] into the forest, putting their own life at risk,” said Ganesh Panta, the chief warden of Chitwan National Park, home to the country’s largest tiger population.

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.31.24-PM-1024x575.png A sign warning of tigers at Kumroj Community Forest in Nepal. Danielle Preiss/The World

Close to the Indian border, the remote Madi Valley is surrounded by the park on almost all sides. Reaching its villages requires driving through the jungle, where langur monkeys, spotted deer and rhinoceros are common sights.

At dusk, Sarita Bhote walked to the edge of her village, Pandav Nagar, to show where the jungle begins. A fence that was meant to separate people from wildlife had been broken by elephants. Rhinos also enter the area, as well as tigers that prey on livestock at night.

Keeping people and wildlife apart is nearly impossible. Just a month earlier, Bhote’s neighbor, Bhanu Bhote, was killed by a tiger while fishing in a nearby river.

“Fishing is the fastest way to earn money here,” Sarita Bhote explained, as a group of her neighbors emerged after fishing in the same river.

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.37.37-PM-1024x600.png Sarita Bhote stands at the edge of her village in Nepal’s Madi Valley. Salim Ali/The World

The dilemma was even clearer one morning in another village, where a group of women had gone to cut elephant grass inside the Kumroj Community Forest. Next to a sign forbidding entry before 10:00 a.m. and after 2:00 p.m. — when tigers are most active — the women climbed over the locked gate.

Museum director Mahato explained that some of the residents have to work other jobs during the day and can’t avoid entering the forest in the morning.

In the buffer zone around the national park, forests like this one are managed by the communities. Local residents can collect resources such as grass and firewood outside the national park’s protected area.

“We are scared. But what can we do? We have to feed our goats and buffaloes,” one woman said.

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.26.42-PM-1024x643.png Water buffalo at Sarita Bhote’s house in Madi Valley, close to Nepal’s border with India. Danielle Preiss/The World

For families who depend on the forest, staying away isn’t an option. But tigers are showing up in these community forests more. They sometimes mistake people bent over cutting grass or collecting firewood for prey. Counterintuitively, conservationists say human disturbance can improve habitat for tiger prey.

Sasank Poudel, the head of wildlife programs at World Wildlife Fund Nepal, said grass-cutting controls invasive plants and stimulates growth that attracts deer. Where prey thrive, tigers follow. One solution is to better manage the habitat deep inside the park.

“If you can, provide enough cover, water and prey species for tigers to remain within the protected areas and within their home ranges and territory, so that they don’t have to venture out of the park, and so that there will be less direct confrontation,” Poudel said.

The government is also hoping to expand wildlife tourism to create alternative sources of income. While Chitwan attracts over 150,000 visitors a year, Panta said places like the Madi Valley have seen little of that tourism.

View Image: 2026-08-06-Nepal-tigers-elephants-1024x576.jpg Chitwan National Park staff patrol the area while riding on elephants, Nepal. Salim Ali/The World

It has transformed Sarita Bhote’s life, who used to collect edible ferns and bamboo shoots from the forest to earn money. She lived in constant fear of encountering tigers or bears, and of not making enough. Today, she runs a homestay for the few visitors who make it to Madi, hoping to spot wildlife. Some of her guests recently saw a tiger on a guided tour.

“I quit going into the jungle,” she said.

But she is one of few entrepreneurs in this isolated valley with limited public infrastructure like roads and reliable electricity. For now, few tourists make the trek through the jungle to reach Madi.

While Nepal’s tigers have made a stunning comeback, the challenge now is making sure the people who live alongside them aren’t left behind.

बीस वर्ष पूर्व बीरेन्द्र महतो चितवन राष्ट्रिय उद्यान के समीप थारु सांस्कृतिक संग्रहालय के स्थापना केने छलाह — नेपाल के पहिल राष्ट्रीय उद्यान आ यूनेस्को के विश्व धरोहर स्थल — एकटा आदिवासी जीवन पद्धति के संरक्षण के लेल जेकरा हुनका आशंका छल जे फीका पड़ि रहल अछि |

भीतर नेपाल के दक्षिणी मैदान के मूल निवासी थारु लोगऽ के प्रथा के प्रदर्शन के साथ-साथ ई याद दिलाबै के साथ बैठलऽ छै कि राष्ट्र के जंगल कखनी देश के अभिजात वर्ग के शिकार के मैदान छेलै ।

महतो न॑ कहलकै कि ई सब कखनी-कखनी बहुत दर्दनाक कहानी होय छै, नेपाल केरऽ एगो पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री केरऽ ३०० बाघऽ के खाल के सामने के फोटो के तरफ इशारा करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै — लगभग उतना ही जेतना कि पिछला बाघ के जनगणना म॑ दर्ज पूरा आबादी ।

ओ कहलनि जे, बाहरी लोक एकटा एहन प्रजाति के बाघ के शिकार क लगभग विलुप्त भ गेल छल जेकर बगल मे थारु बहुत दिन स रहैत छल।

“किछु साल तक हम सब अपन रिश्तेदार, अपन पूर्वज के बाघ स’ गंवा देलहुं, मुदा हमरा सब के कोनो दिक्कत नहि भेल, कारण हमर पूर्वज सोचने छलाह: “हम सब एकहि इलाका मे रहैत छी, ओही क्षेत्र मे. कखनो बाघ हमरा सब लेल [हानिकारक] होइत अछि, कखनो हम बाघ लेल हानिकारक छी।'

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.34.33-PM-1024x670.png नेपाल के चितवन राष्ट्रिय उद्यान के पास थारु सांस्कृतिक संग्रहालय के बाहर बिरेन्द्र महतो खड़ा। डैनियल प्रिस/द वर्ल्ड

शिकार आ आवासक क्षति नेपाल आ विश्व भरि मे बाघक आबादी नष्ट कएने छल । मुदा दशकों के गिरावट के बाद नेपाल दुनिया के सबस सफल बाघ रिकवरी में स एक के शुरुआत केलक। 2010 मे नेपाल 12 अन्य देशक संग 2022 धरि अपन संख्या दुगुना करबाक वचन देलक — नेपाल एकर बदला मे लगभग तीन गुना बढ़ेलक । मुदा आब स्थानीय लोक शिकारी के संग सह-अस्तित्व मे संघर्ष क रहल छथिन्ह.

जेना-जेना बाघ के संख्या बढ़ल अछि, लोक सं घातक मुठभेड़ के चिंता सेहो बढ़ल अछि. पंता के कहनाय छनि जे एकर समाधान अछि जे बाघ के संरक्षित क्षेत्र मे राखल जाए आओर ओहि सं बाहर के लोक के रोजी-रोटी के साधन सेहो बनाओल जाए.

देश केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ बाघऽ के आबादी वाला चितवन नेशनल पार्क केरऽ मुख्य वार्डन गणेश पंता न॑ कहलकै कि हम्में स्थानीय समुदाय क॑ वू तरह स॑ सहयोग करै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छियै ताकि ओकरा जंगल म॑ [प्रवेश] के जरूरत नै पड़॑, जेकरा स॑ ओकरऽ खुद के जान खतरा म॑ पड़॑ सक॑ ।

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.31.24-PM-1024x575.png नेपाल के कुमरोज सामुदायिक वन में बाघ के चेतावनी के एक साइन। डैनियल प्रिस/द वर्ल्ड

भारतीय सीमाक नजदीक सुदूर मादी घाटी लगभग चारू कात पार्क सं घेरल अछि. एकरऽ गाँवऽ में पहुँचै लेली जंगलऽ के बीच स॑ गाड़ी चलाबै के जरूरत छै, जहां लंगुर बानर, धब्बेदार हिरण आरू गैंडा आम दृश्य छै ।

गोधूलि बेला मे सरिता भोते अपन गामक किनार पांडव नगर दिस बढ़लीह जे जंगल कतय सँ शुरू होइत छैक से देखाबय लेल। एकटा बाड़ जे लोक के वन्यजीव स अलग करबाक छल, हाथी तोड़ि देने छल। गैंडा सेहो एहि इलाका मे प्रवेश करैत अछि, संगहि बाघ सेहो जे राति मे पशुधनक शिकार करैत अछि ।

लोक आ वन्यजीव के अलग राखब लगभग असंभव अछि. मात्र एक मास पहिने भोटे के पड़ोसी भानु भोटे के पास के नदी में माछ मारय के दौरान बाघ के मौत भ गेल छल.

“एतय पाइ कमयबाक सबसँ तेज तरीका अछि माछ मारब” सरिता भोटे बतौलनि, जखन कि ओही नदी मे माछ मारलाक बाद ओकर पड़ोसीक एकटा समूह उभरल छल ।

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.37.37-PM-1024x600.png सरिता भोटे नेपालक माडी उपत्यका मे अपन गामक किनार पर ठाढ़ छथि । सलीम अली/द वर्ल्ड

एक दिन भोरे दोसर गाम मे दुविधा आओर साफ भ गेल छल, जतय कुमरोज सामुदायिक वन के भीतर हाथी घास काटय लेल महिला के एकटा समूह गेल छल. 10:00 बजे सं पहिने आ 2:00 बजे के बाद प्रवेश पर रोक लगाबय वाला बोर्ड के बगल में. — जखन बाघ बेसी सक्रिय होइत अछि — महिला सभ ताला लागल गेट पर चढ़ि गेलीह ।

संग्रहालय के निदेशक महतो बतौलनि जे किछु निवासी के दिन में दोसर काज करय पड़ैत छनि आ भोरे जंगल में प्रवेश सं बाचि नहिं सकैत छथि.

नेशनल पार्क के आसपास के बफर जोन में एहि तरहक जंगल के प्रबंधन समुदाय द्वारा कयल जाइत अछि | स्थानीय निवासी राष्ट्रीय उद्यान कें संरक्षित क्षेत्र सं बाहर घास आ जलाऊ लकड़ी जैना संसाधनक कें संग्रहण कयर सकय छै.

ओ कहला जे हम सब डरा गेल छी। मुदा हम की क सकैत छी। हमरा सभकेँ अपन बकरी-भैंसकेँ खुआबए पड़त।'' एकटा महिला बजलीह।

View Image: Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-7.26.42-PM-1024x643.png नेपाल के भारत के सीमा के नजदीक माडी घाटी में सरिता भोटे के घर पर जल भैंस | डैनियल प्रिस/द वर्ल्ड

जंगल पर निर्भर परिवार’क लेल दूर रहब कोनो विकल्प नहिं. मुदा एहि सामुदायिक जंगल मे बाघ बेसी देखा रहल अछि। ओ सभ कखनो काल घास काटि कए वा जलाऊ लकड़ी जमा करबा पर झुकल लोक कए शिकार क लेल गलती करैत छथि । एकरऽ विपरीत रूप स॑ संरक्षणवादी के कहना छै कि मानव गड़बड़ी स॑ बाघ के शिकार के आवास म॑ सुधार आबी सकै छै ।

विश्व वन्यजीव कोष नेपालक वन्यजीव कार्यक्रम प्रमुख सासंक पौडेल घास काटला सँ आक्रामक पौधा पर नियंत्रण होइत अछि आ मृग के आकर्षित करय बला विकास के उत्तेजित होइत अछि से बतौलनि । जतय शिकार पनपैत अछि ओतय बाघ सेहो पाछू पड़ैत अछि । एकरऽ एगो उपाय ई छै कि पार्क केरऽ गहराई म॑ आवास केरऽ बेहतर प्रबंधन करलऽ जाय ।

पौडेल कहलकै, “जदि आपने करी सकै छियै त॑ बाघऽ लेली पर्याप्त आवरण, पानी आरू शिकार के प्रजाति उपलब्ध कराबै कि वू संरक्षित क्षेत्रऽ के भीतर आरू अपनऽ घरऽ के सीमा आरू इलाका के भीतर रह॑ सक॑, ताकि ओकरा पार्क स॑ बाहर निकलै के साहस नै करलऽ जाय, आरू ताकि सीधा मुठभेड़ कम होय सक॑ ।

सरकार के उम्मीद सेहो अछि जे वन्यजीव पर्यटन के विस्तार करि आमदनी के वैकल्पिक स्रोत पैदा कएल जाएत. चितवन म॑ जहां साल म॑ डेढ़ लाख स॑ भी अधिक लोग आबै छै, वहीं पंता न॑ कहलकै कि माडी घाटी जैसनऽ जगहऽ प॑ वू पर्यटन केरऽ कम देखलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ओ बजलीह, “हम जंगल मे जेनाइ छोड़ि देलियैक।

title: Nepal wants to become vibrant bridge connecting India, China: FM Khanal - dailyexcelsior.com
description: Nepal wants to become vibrant bridge connecting India, China: FM Khanal  dailyexcelsior.com
publisher.title: dailyexcelsior.com
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Aug 7 : Nepal wants to transform itself from a landlocked country into a "vibrant, dynamic bridge" connecting India and China, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said here on Friday.

Nepal welcomed the continued development and prosperity of both India and China, Khanal said as he inaugurated a two-day international conference titled 'China and South Asia in a Multipolar World.'

The foreign minister added that Nepal remained committed to strengthening its relations with both its neighbours based on "sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns."

The conference was jointly organised by the Centre for South Asian Studies, Fudan University, China, and Nepal Institute for International Cooperation and Engagement.

The remarks assume significance as Nepal's new government led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah has sought to pursue a balanced foreign policy towards its two immediate neighbours while placing greater emphasis on economic diplomacy, investment and connectivity.

"Asia's transformation presents unprecedented opportunities for shared prosperity," Khanal said, stressing that South Asia possesses enormous promise, although much of its economic potential remains untapped.

He said economic diplomacy had become "one of the defining priorities" of Nepal's external engagement and that the country's foreign policy was aimed at improving the lives of its people through trade, investment, employment, tourism, technology, innovation and sustainable development.

"Nepal sincerely welcomes the continued development and prosperity of both India and China and remains committed to further strengthening its longstanding bilateral relations with both neighbours independently, on the basis of sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns," he said.

"Nepal aspires to transform itself from a landlocked country into a vibrant, dynamic bridge connecting China and India," Khanal added.

Khanal's back-to-back visits to New Delhi and Beijing in June were seen as an early indication of Kathmandu's effort to maintain balanced ties with both neighbours.

He had earlier said Nepal wants to build stronger and deeper relations with both India and China, describing the southern and northern neighbours as vital partners for the Himalayan nation. (PTI)

title: HIB to be reformed as original Nepali model - The Rising Nepal
description: HIB to be reformed as original Nepali model  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 8: Dr. Subash Pyakurel was appointed as the Chairman of the Health Insurance Board (HIB) last week. Dr. Pyakurel has taken over the responsibility of the board at a time when it is probably in its most critical state ever.

Looking back a few months ago, many had pointed out that the health insurance programme being operated by the government could be scrapped. Meanwhile, many experts are urging the government to improve the health insurance system.

Earlier, a task force formed by the Health Ministry drafted a new modality for the Health Insurance Board. Experts argue that the new Board has many challenges to reform it.

Chairman Dr. Pyakurel informed that the HIB will be reformed as a one-door system, incorporating various sectors and social security programmes including Ama Surakshya, civil servants, Nepali Army, and Nepal Police.

“I was personally involved in the process of reforming the Health Insurance Board. Based on that experience and international best practices, we are now developing our own original model of health insurance. In the meantime, we have reviewed various insurance models used in many countries. Drawing from these best practices, we aim to introduce our own insurance model. However, we will need at least one year for the preparation,” said Dr. Pyakurel.

Dr. Pyakurel added that the newly formed board is first preparing to digitize all its services. Before this, the board is making a four-digit hotline number public within a few days.

He stated that the new system would make it easier for the general public to inquire about the services provided by the insurance board and to file complaints. He also mentioned that through digitization, the board will be able to offer numerous services in a more accessible manner.

During the government led by Sushila Karki, various challenges were identified, including financial burdens, service leakage, misuse of services, a limited group of beneficiaries, and passive beneficiaries.

To deal with those challenges, the government initiated to reform the Health Insurance Board, aiming to expand its services. However, many hospitals and health institutions withdrew from the insurance service, demanding billions of rupees in lump sum payments.

This created an additional challenge for the government. Along with the challenge of having to pay billions of rupees to the hospitals, the government faced a huge challenge of how to continue the insurance programme.

In the meantime, the government formed multiple task forces and invited experts to reform the HIB. A common suggestion from many experts and task forces was to prevent financial burden and create a one-door system.

The new framework of the HIB aims to reduce the growing financial burden, prevent leakage, implement an integrated payment system, and transform insurance into a real insurance model.

The government has announced a comprehensive restructuring of the national health insurance programme through the budget and policies and programmes for the fiscal year 2026/27.

According to Dr. Manohar Pradhan, advisor to the Minister of Health and Food Safety, the government is implementing comprehensive reforms to strengthen and modernize the national health insurance system by introducing an Integrated Payment System (IPS), which brings together various fragmented social health security programmes and government health obligations under a single umbrella.

Through this system, all medical expenses and health-related programmes financed by the Social Security Fund will be managed through a one-door payment mechanism coordinated by the Health Insurance Board, improving efficiency, accountability, and service delivery.

At the same time, the existing programme is being transformed from a predominantly social security model into a contribution-based real insurance model, where high- and middle-income citizens will pay income-based premiums under a graded contribution system and receive benefits accordingly, while the government will continue to fully subsidize premiums for poor households, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and Dalit communities to ensure equitable access to healthcare.

In addition, to ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the health insurance programme, the government has developed a financing framework aimed at reducing financial deficits and ensuring the timely reimbursement of hospitals, including allocating a designated share of taxes collected from alcohol and tobacco products to the Health Insurance Fund.

These reforms collectively represent a major step toward building a more efficient, equitable, financially sustainable, and digitally enabled national health insurance system, with the government setting an ambitious target of extending health insurance coverage to 90 per cent of the Nepali population within the next three years.

Dr. Pradhan stated that experts and government officials have reviewed various best practices from countries such as Canada, Cuba, the United States, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, India, and other African nations. Based on these practices, the government is working to develop a new model for insurance services, Dr. Pradhan mentioned.

“In line with the spirit of the government and the expectations of the citizens, we must make insurance services accessible, effective and sustainable. For this, we are working with advice and suggestions from all relevant sectors, not just one individual or group,” said Dr. Pradhan.

डॉ. प्याकुरेल कहलनि जे, हम व्यक्तिगत रूप स स्वास्थ्य बीमा बोर्ड मे सुधार क प्रक्रिया मे शामिल छलहुं।ओहि अनुभव आ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सर्वोत्तम प्रथा क आधार पर आब हम सब स्वास्थ्य बीमा क अपन मूल मॉडल तैयार क रहल छी।एहि बीच हम सब कईटा देश मे उपयोग कैल जाय वाला विभिन्न बीमा मॉडल क समीक्षा केलहुं अछि। एहि सर्वोत्तम प्रथा स आकर्षित भ हमर सबहक लक्ष्य अछि जे हम अपन बीमा मॉडल शुरू करी।हालांकि तैयारी लेल हमरा सब कए कम स कम एक साल क जरूरत पड़त।

डॉ. प्याकुरेल न॑ आरू कहलकै कि नवगठित बोर्ड सबसें पहल॑ अपनऽ सब सेवा क॑ डिजिटल करै के तैयारी करी रहलऽ छै । एहि सं पहिने बोर्ड किछ दिन मे चारि अंक के हॉटलाइन नंबर के सार्वजनिक क रहल अछि.

ओ कहला जे एहि नव व्यवस्था स आम जनता कए बीमा बोर्ड क सेवा क बारे मे पूछताछ करबा मे आ शिकायत दर्ज करबा मे आसानी होएत। हुनी ई भी बतैलकै कि डिजिटाइजेशन के माध्यम स॑ बोर्ड अधिक सुलभ तरीका स॑ अनेक सेवा प्रदान करी सकै छै ।

सुशीला कार्की के नेतृत्व में सरकार के दौरान विभिन्न चुनौती के पहचान कायल गेल, जाहि में आर्थिक बोझ, सेवा रिसाव, सेवा के दुरुपयोग, लाभार्थी के सीमित समूह, आ निष्क्रिय लाभार्थी शामिल छल।

ओहि चुनौतियक स निपटबा लेल सरकार स्वास्थ्य बीमा बोर्ड मे सुधार क शुरुआत केलक, जेकर उद्देश्य छल ओकर सेवा क विस्तार। मुदा, अरबों रुपैया एकमुश्त भुगतान के मांग करैत कतेको अस्पताल आ स्वास्थ्य संस्थान बीमा सेवा सं हटि गेल.

एहि स सरकार लेल एकटा अतिरिक्त चुनौती पैदा भ गेल। अस्पताल कए अरबों रुपया देबय पड़य के चुनौती के संग संग सरकार के सामने एकटा पैघ चुनौती छल जे बीमा कार्यक्रम के कोना जारी राखल जाए.

एहि बीच सरकार कईटा टास्क फोर्स क गठन केलक आ एचआईबी मे सुधार लेल विशेषज्ञ कए आमंत्रित केलक। बहुत विशेषज्ञ आरू टास्क फोर्स केरऽ एगो आम सुझाव छेलै कि आर्थिक बोझ क॑ रोकी क॑ एक दरवाजा वाला सिस्टम बनालऽ जाय ।

एचआईबी कें नव ढाँचा कें उद्देश्य बढ़ैत वित्तीय बोझ कें कम करनाय, रिसाव कें रोकनाय, एकीकृत भुगतान प्रणाली कें लागू करनाय, आ बीमा कें वास्तविक बीमा मॉडल मे बदलनाय छै.

सरकार वित्तीय वर्ष 2026/27 के लेल बजट आ पॉलिसी आ कार्यक्रम के माध्यम सं राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य बीमा कार्यक्रम के व्यापक पुनर्गठन के घोषणा केलक अछि.

स्वास्थ्य आरू खाद्य सुरक्षा मंत्री के सलाहकार डॉ. मनोहर प्रधान के अनुसार सरकार एकीकृत भुगतान प्रणाली (आईपीएस) शुरू करी क राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य बीमा प्रणाली क मजबूत आरू आधुनिक बनाबै लेली व्यापक सुधार लागू करी रहलौ छै, जेकरा मँ विभिन्न खंडित सामाजिक स्वास्थ्य सुरक्षा कार्यक्रम आरू सरकारी स्वास्थ्य दायित्व क एक छत्रछाया मँ एक साथ लानलऽ जाय छै ।

अइ प्रणाली कें माध्यम सं सामाजिक सुरक्षा कोष दूवारा वित्तपोषित सबटा चिकित्सा व्ययक आ स्वास्थ्य सं संबंधित कार्यक्रमक कें प्रबंधन स्वास्थ्य बीमा बोर्ड कें समन्वय सं एक दरवाजा कें भुगतान तंत्र कें माध्यम सं कैल जेतय, जे दक्षता, जवाबदेही, आ सेवा प्रदायगी मे सुधार करतय.

एकर संग-संग मौजूदा कार्यक्रम कें मुख्य रूप सं सामाजिक सुरक्षा मॉडल सं योगदान आधारित वास्तविक बीमा मॉडल मे बदलल जा रहल छै, जत उच्च आ मध्यम आय वाला नागरिक ग्रेडेड योगदान प्रणाली कें तहत आय आधारित प्रीमियम कें भुगतान करतय आ तदनुसार लाभ प्राप्त करतय, जखन कि सरकार स्वास्थ्य देखभाल कें समान पहुंच सुनिश्चित करय कें लेल गरीब घरक, वरिष्ठ नागरिकक, दिव्यांग व्यक्तियक, आ दलित समुदायक कें लेल प्रीमियम कें पूर्ण रूप सं सब्सिडी जारी रखतय.

एकर अलावा स्वास्थ्य बीमा कार्यक्रम कें दीर्घकालिक वित्तीय स्थायित्व सुनिश्चित करय कें लेल सरकार एकटा वित्तपोषण ढाँचा तैयार करलक छै जेकर उद्देश्य वित्तीय घाटा कें कम करनाय आ अस्पतालक कें समय पर प्रतिपूर्ति सुनिश्चित करनाय छै, जइ मे शराब आ तंबाकू उत्पादक सं एकत्रित कर कें निर्धारित हिस्सा कें स्वास्थ्य बीमा कोष मे आवंटित करनाय शामिल छै.

इ सुधार सामूहिक रूप सं एकटा बेसि कुशल, न्यायसंगत, आर्थिक रूप सं टिकाऊ, आ डिजिटल रूप सं सक्षम राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य बीमा प्रणाली कें निर्माण कें दिशा मे एकटा पैघ कदम कें प्रतिनिधित्व करय छै, जइ मे सरकार अगिला तीन सालक कें भीतर स्वास्थ्य बीमा कवरेज कें 90 प्रतिशत नेपाली आबादी तइक विस्तारित करय कें महत्वाकांक्षी लक्ष्य निर्धारित करय छै.

डॉ. प्रधान न॑ कहलकै कि विशेषज्ञ आरू सरकारी अधिकारी न॑ कनाडा, क्यूबा, ​​अमेरिका, जापान, थाईलैंड, इंडोनेशिया, भारत, आरू अन्य अफ्रीकी राष्ट्र जैसनऽ देशऽ के विभिन्न सर्वोत्तम प्रथा के समीक्षा करल॑ छै । एहि प्रथा क आधार पर सरकार बीमा सेवा क लेल एकटा नव मॉडल तैयार करबा मे लागल अछि, डॉ. प्रधान उल्लेख केलथि।

डॉ. प्रधान कहलनि जे, सरकार के भावना आ नागरिक के अपेक्षा के अनुरूप हमरा सब के बीमा सेवा के सुलभ, प्रभावी आ टिकाऊ बनाबय पड़त, एकरा लेल हम सब संबंधित क्षेत्र के सलाह आ सुझाव के संग काज क रहल छी, सिर्फ एकटा व्यक्ति या समूह के नहि।

title: One in three police units lack own buildings - The Rising Nepal
description: One in three police units lack own buildings  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 8: Nearly one in three Nepal Police units across the country are operating without their own office buildings, while growing public demand for police services in remote areas has prompted local communities to donate land for new police posts.

According to Nepal Police Headquarters, the force currently operates 2,660 police units nationwide. Of these, only 1,884 have their own buildings, while the remaining 776 operate without permanent office infrastructure. Among them, 363 function from rented premises and another 418 are housed in buildings provided by other government agencies.

Addressing a press conference on Friday, Nepal Police Central Spokesperson and Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Abi Narayan Kafle said the organisation continued to face serious infrastructure and manpower constraints despite increasing public support for expanding police services.

Residents across the country have so far donated 107 ropanis of private land free of charge for the construction of police offices, while formal proposals have been submitted seeking the establishment of 970 new police units.

"In many places, local people have voluntarily offered land because they want police services within their communities," DIG Kafle said, adding that the initiative reflected growing public confidence in Nepal Police and increasing awareness of the importance of police presence in local communities.

Demand for new police units has come from every province, including 254 in Koshi, 100 in Madhes, 123 in Bagmati, 75 in Gandaki, 174 in Lumbini, 84 in Karnali, 139 in Sudurpaschim and 21 in the Kathmandu Valley.

Police officials said expanding their presence had become increasingly important as the organisation's responsibilities continued to widen. Besides maintaining law and order, the force is now expected to investigate cybercrime, combat organised criminal activities, respond to natural disasters, conduct rescue operations and strengthen community policing.

However, the organisation said meeting public expectations would be difficult with its existing resources. Establishing and operating all the proposed police units would require more than 17,100 additional police personnel.

Nepal Police has an approved strength of 79,531 personnel, but 4,837 posts remain vacant, limiting its capacity to deploy officers to new locations and strengthen policing in underserved areas.

The organisation is also working to increase women's participation in policing. Nepal Police currently employs 9,841 women officers, accounting for nearly 13 per cent of its total workforce. Police said women officers have played an increasingly important role in handling cases involving women and children, investigating domestic violence and expanding community outreach programmes.

During the review period, disciplinary action was taken against 1,460 police personnel, while 606 officers received rewards for outstanding performance. Police also reported resolving more than 99 per cent of the 3,753 complaints lodged against its personnel.

According to police statistics, 60,016 criminal cases were registered during the last fiscal year. While incidents of murder and robbery declined, cases involving narcotics, cybercrime, banking fraud, theft and illegal firearms increased. Police arrested 19,518 individuals in connection with those offences.

The force also registered 14,911 complaints of domestic violence and said it was expanding public awareness campaigns and victim-support programmes.

Road safety remains another major concern. Nepal Police recorded an average of 82 road accidents every day during the review period, resulting in about 130 injuries and seven deaths daily.

Nearly 30,000 people are injured in road crashes each year, with speeding, reckless driving, increasing traffic volume and poor road conditions identified as the principal causes.

Presenting the organisation's annual performance review, DIG Kafle said Nepal Police would continue prioritising improvements in infrastructure, personnel management and service delivery to meet the growing expectations of citizens and ensure effective policing across the country.

डीआईजी काफ्ले कहलनि जे, बहुत ठाम स्थानीय लोक स्वेच्छा स जमीन के प्रस्ताव देलक अछि, किया कि हुनका अपन समुदाय के भीतर पुलिस सेवा चाही।

कोशी मे 254, मधेश मे 100, बागमती मे 123, गंडकी मे 75, लुम्बिनी मे 174, कर्णाली मे 84, सुदुरपश्चिम मे 139 आ काठमांडू उपत्यका मे 21 सहित नव प्रहरी इकाई क मांग प्रत्येक प्रदेश स आयल अछि।

पुलिस अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे संगठन के जिम्मेदारी बढ़ैत रहला सं हुनकर उपस्थिति बढ़ाबय के महत्व बढ़ि गेल अछि. कानून व्यवस्था कायम रखबाक अलावा आब एहि बल स साइबर अपराध क जांच, संगठित आपराधिक गतिविधि क मुकाबला, प्राकृतिक आपदा क जवाब, बचाव अभियान आ सामुदायिक पुलिसिंग कए मजबूत करबाक उम्मीद अछि।

मुदा संस्था के कहनाय अछि जे अपन मौजूदा संसाधन सं जन अपेक्षा के पूरा करब मुश्किल होएत. सबटा प्रस्तावित पुलिस यूनिट क स्थापना आ संचालन मे 17,100 स बेसी अतिरिक्त पुलिस कर्मी क जरूरत होएत।

संस्था पुलिसिंग मे महिला के भागीदारी बढ़ाबय के काज सेहो क रहल अछि. नेपाल प्रहरीमे एखन ९,८४१ महिला अधिकारी कार्यरत अछि, जे ओकर कुल कार्यबल के लगभग १३ प्रतिशत अछि । पुलिस के कहनाय छनि जे महिला आ बच्चा सं जुड़ल मामला के निपटारा... घरेलू हिंसा के जांच आओर सामुदायिक आउटरीच कार्यक्रम के विस्तार मे महिला अधिकारी के भूमिका तेजी सं बढ़ल अछि.

समीक्षा अवधि मे 1460 पुलिसकर्मी क खिलाफ अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई कैल गेल, जखन कि 606 अधिकारी कए उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शन क इनाम देल गेल। पुलिस अपन कर्मी के खिलाफ दर्ज 3753 शिकायत मे सं 99 प्रतिशत सं बेसि शिकायत के निपटारा करय के सेहो खबर देलक अछि.

संस्थाके वार्षिक प्रदर्शन समीक्षा प्रस्तुत करैत डीआईजी काफ्ले कहलनि जे, नेपाल पुलिस नागरिकक बढैत अपेक्षा के पूरा करय आ देश भरि मे प्रभावी पुलिसिंग सुनिश्चित करबाक लेल बुनियादी ढांचा, कार्मिक प्रबंधन आ सेवा प्रदायगी मे सुधार के प्राथमिकता दैत रहत।

title: Rs. 250 shopping bill turns into Rs. 1 million windfall - The Rising Nepal
description: Rs. 250 shopping bill turns into Rs. 1 million windfall  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter,Kathmandu, Aug. 8: The Taxpayer Incentive Reward Programme announced by the government through the budget for the current fiscal year has officially begun.

The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) on Friday announced the first winners of the government's Taxpayer Incentive Reward Programme, unveiling the results of the first fortnightly bumper draw for the month of Shrawan.

According to the Department, a consumer who purchased goods worth Rs. 250 from Shiva Krishna General Store in Punarbas Municipality, Kanchanpur, won the Rs. 1 million bumper prize.

The winning coupon number is 007 315 254 493.

According to the IRD, the winning purchase was made on July 23, 2026.

Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle announced the results at a programme held at the Ministry of Finance in Kathmandu.

In addition to the bumper prize winner, 15 consumers each won Rs. 100,000 after tax in the first fortnightly draw.

Under the programme, 15 consumers are awarded Rs. 133,334 each in every fortnightly draw. In addition, one bumper prize winner receives Rs. 1 million every 15 days.

A 25 per cent tax on windfall gains, as stipulated in the Income Tax Act, 2002 (2058 BS), will be deducted from the prize money before payment.

The government introduced the Taxpayers' Incentive Reward Programme through the budget for the current fiscal year to encourage consumers to demand VAT bills while making purchases and to strengthen tax compliance.

This programme has been introduced with the objective of making the economy formal and transparent by encouraging the culture of receiving and giving bills in the purchase and sale of goods and services.

The government aims to develop Value Added Tax (VAT) as a sustainable source of revenue.

To facilitate participation, the IRD has launched the prize.ird.gov.np portal, where eligible consumers can upload their purchase bills.

Consumers who make cash purchases of goods or services worth more than Rs. 100 within Nepal for personal use and obtain an original VAT bill are eligible to participate.

According to the IRD, consumers who purchase goods or services worth more than Rs. 100 using QR payments through banks or digital wallets are currently not required to register their bills.

The Ministry of Finance approved the Taxpayers' Incentive Reward Programme Operation Guidelines in mid-July.

According to Keshav Raghuvanshi, Information Officer and Director of the IRD, the coupon numbers and brief details of the selected winners will be published on the Department's website.

Keeping personal privacy in mind, the full name and mobile number of the winner have not been made public.

The Department said that prize winners can claim their cash rewards by visiting the nearest Inland Revenue Office within 15 days, carrying their original VAT bills and other required documents

title: ‘Old is Gold’ film screening begins with Aama - The Rising Nepal
description: ‘Old is Gold’ film screening begins with Aama  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Aug. 8: Film Development Board (FDB), Nepal, has launched its new ‘Old is Gold’ film series with a special screening of Aama, the first Nepali-language feature film.

Aama was directed by Hira Singh Khatri. The film was written by Durga Shrestha and Chaitya Devi. It was produced by King Mahendra under the Information Department of the Government of Nepal (formerly the Royal Nepal Film Corporation).

Artists including Shiva Shankar Manandhar and Bhuwan Chand were in leading roles, while Basundhara Bhusal, Chaitya Devi Singh, Hira Singh Khatri and Hari Prasad Rimal played supporting roles.

In the event, veteran actors Bhuwan Chand, Chaitya Devi Singh, Basundhara Bhusal and Bimala Shrestha attended the opening programme.

The cinema hall was full, and some people had to watch the film while standing because there were not enough seats.

The programme began with actor Hari Bansha Acharya and former Film Development Board Chairman Krishna Malla welcoming the four veteran actors with flower garlands. The guests then lit a traditional oil lamp to officially open the event.

FDB Chairman Dinesh DC hosted the programme. Before the screening, he spoke with the actors about the making of Aama, its release and their memories of the early days of the Nepali film industry.

The actors shared their experiences of working on the landmark film and spoke about the challenges of filmmaking in those early years.

The event became an emotional occasion as the actors watched the film they had appeared in decades ago on the big screen once again. Many young people also joined older viewers to experience one of Nepal's most important films.

During the programme, Dinesh DC announced that the Board would hold a special screening of one classic Nepali film every month. He said that all income from the screenings would be placed in the Film Workers' Welfare Fund.

According to the Board, the ‘Old is Gold’ series aims to introduce classic Nepali films to younger generations, honour the artists and technicians who helped create them, and preserve Nepal's film heritage.

According to FDB, the screenings began on Friday with Aama. Sindoor, directed by Prakash Thapa, and Parivartan, directed by Hira Singh Khatri, will be screened on Saturday.

The programme will continue on Sunday with Manko Bandh, directed by Prakash Thapa, and Ke Ghar Ke Dera, directed by Pradeep Rijal. On Monday, audiences can watch Kumari, directed by Prem Bahadur Basnyat.

Tuesday's programme includes Shantideep, directed by Laxminath Sharma, followed by Hijo Aaja Bholi, directed by Hira Singh Khatri.

The film series will conclude on Wednesday with Badalindo Aakash, directed by Laxminath Sharma, and Jeevan Rekha, directed by Prakash Thapa.

एक स्टाफ रिपोर्टर, काठमांडू, ८ अगस्त : नेपाल के फिल्म विकास बोर्ड (एफडीबी) नेपाली भाषा के पहिल फीचर फिल्म आमा के विशेष प्रदर्शन के साथ अपन नया ‘ओल्ड इज गोल्ड’ फिल्म सीरीज के शुभारंभ करलौ गेलौ छै ।

आमा के निर्देशन हीरा सिंह खत्री केने छलाह। ई फिल्म दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ आ चैत्य देवी के लिखल छल । एकर निर्माण राजा महेन्द्र द्वारा नेपाल सरकारक सूचना विभाग (पहिने रॉयल नेपाल फिल्म निगम)क अन्तर्गत भेल छल ।

शिवशंकर मानन्धर आ भुवन चंद सहित कलाकार मुख्य भूमिका मे छलाह, जखन कि बसुंधरा भूसल, चैत्य देवी सिंह, हीरा सिंह खत्री आ हरि प्रसाद रिमाल सहायक भूमिका मे छलाह ।

एहि आयोजन मे उद्घाटन कार्यक्रम मे दिग्गज अभिनेता भुवन चंद, चैत्य देवी सिंह, बसुंधरा भुसाल आ बिमला श्रेष्ठ शामिल छलाह ।

सिनेमा हॉल भरि गेल छल, आ किछु लोक केँ ठाढ़ भ' क' फिल्म देखय पड़ैत छल, कारण सीट पर्याप्त नहि छल.

कार्यक्रम केरऽ शुरुआत अभिनेता हरि बंशा आचार्य आरू फिल्म विकास बोर्ड केरऽ पूर्व अध्यक्ष कृष्ण मल्ल न॑ चारो दिग्गज अभिनेता के फूलऽ के माला स॑ स्वागत करी क॑ करलऽ गेलै । एकर बाद अतिथि सब पारंपरिक तेल दीपक जरा कए आयोजन क आधिकारिक उद्घाटन केलथि।

कार्यक्रम के मेजबानी एफडीबी के अध्यक्ष दिनेश डीसी केलखिन्ह. प्रदर्शन स पहिने ओ अभिनेता सब स आम के निर्माण, एकर रिलीज आ नेपाली फिल्म उद्योग के शुरुआती दिन के याद के बारे में बात केलनि।

अभिनेता सब एहि मील के पत्थर फिल्म पर काज करय के अपन अनुभव साझा केलनि आ ओहि शुरुआती साल मे फिल्म निर्माण के चुनौती के बारे मे बजलाह.

ई आयोजन एकटा भावुक अवसर बनि गेल, कारण अभिनेता लोकनि एक बेर फेर पैघ पर्दा पर दशकों पहिने जे फिल्म देखल गेल छलाह, ओकरा देखलनि। नेपाल के एकटा महत्वपूर्ण फिल्म के अनुभव करय लेल बहुत रास युवा सेहो पैघ दर्शक के संग जुड़ल छलाह.

कार्यक्रम के दौरान दिनेश डीसी घोषणा केलनि जे बोर्ड हर महीना एकटा क्लासिक नेपाली फिल्म के विशेष प्रदर्शन करत। ओ कहला जे एहि प्रदर्शन स जे आमदनी होएत ओ सबटा फिल्म मजदूर कल्याण कोष मे राखल जाएत।

बोर्ड के अनुसार ‘ओल्ड इज गोल्ड’ सीरीज के उद्देश्य छै कि क्लासिक नेपाली फिल्म के युवा पीढ़ी के परिचय देना, ओकरा बनाबै में मदद करै वाला कलाकार आरू तकनीशियन के सम्मानित करना, आरू नेपाल के फिल्म धरोहर के संरक्षण करना छै ।

एफडीबी के अनुसार शुक्रदिन आमा के संग स्क्रीनिंग शुरू भेल छल. प्रकाश थापा निर्देशित सिन्दूर आ हीरा सिंह खत्री के निर्देशन में परिवर्तन के प्रदर्शन शनिदिन होयत।

कार्यक्रम रविदिन प्रकाश थापा के निर्देशन में मनको बंध आ प्रदीप रिजाल के निर्देशन में के घर के डेरा के संग जारी रहत। सोमदिन दर्शक प्रेम बहादुर बसन्यत के निर्देशन में बनल कुमारी देख सकैत छथि।

मंगलदिन के कार्यक्रम में लक्ष्मीनाथ शर्मा के निर्देशन में शांतिदीप, ओकर बाद हीरा सिंह खत्री के निर्देशन में हिजो आजा भोली शामिल अछि.

बुधदिन लक्ष्मीनाथ शर्मा निर्देशित बादलिन्दो आकाश आ प्रकाश थापा निर्देशित जीवन रेखा के संग फिल्म श्रृंखला के समापन होयत।

publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Aug. 8: The National Sports Council (NSC) has launched a closed-door training camp for athletes and coaches selected to represent Nepal at the upcoming 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

According to Sikka Suwal Shrestha, an executive committee member of the NSC, the camp commenced on 3 August.

The participating contingent has been accommodated across two capital venues: the Royal Boutique Hotel in Sinamangal and the Pashupati Boutique Hotel in Gaushala.

The Royal Boutique Hotel is hosting athletes and coaching staff in judo, wushu, women’s volleyball, boxing, karate (kata team), dance sports, cycling, golf, athletics, and archery. Meanwhile, the Pashupati Boutique Hotel is accommodating teams in karate (kumite team), taekwondo, soft tennis, tennis, swimming, squash, badminton, and table tennis.Selected athletes in wushu, cycling, golf, taekwondo, tennis, swimming, and table tennis are currently undertaking training abroad.

Athletes in skateboarding, wrestling, canoeing, and men’s and women’s kabaddi are also completing overseas preparatory camps.

The 20th Asian Games will run from 19 September to 4 October in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Nepal will field 136 athletes, 80 men and 56 women, across 22 disciplines.

Boxing squad to train in India

As part of preparations for the Games, a nine-member Nepali boxing delegation, including seven athletes, will be departing for Guwahati, Assam, on 10 August for a 40-day intensive camp at the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) National Centre of Excellence.

Nepal Boxing Association (NBA) Secretary Pushkar Raj Panta confirmed that the team will train in Guwahati until departing directly for Japan ahead of the Games.

The squad features four male and three female boxers.

In men's division, there are Chandra Bahadur Thapa (under-55 kg), Khagendra Roka Magar (under-60 kg), Dan Bahadur Darlami (under-70 kg), and Rabin Nepal (under-90 kg).

In women's division, there are Ramisha Shrestha (under-51 kg), Asmita Tamang (under-54 kg), and Kusum Tamang (under-65 kg).

Rabin Nepal is the sole returning veteran from the 19th Asian Games, whilst the remaining six boxers will be making their Asiad debuts.

The squad features historic medallist Chandra Bahadur Thapa, who secured a bronze medal in the men’s under-54 kg weight class at the 2025 IBA World Boxing Championships in Dubai, the highest international achievement in Nepali boxing history.

Coaches Raj Shrestha and Deepak Maharjan will oversee training, with NBA General Secretary Man Bahadur Bhandari serving as team manager.

Bhandari is scheduled to join the squad in India at a later date.

Boxing most successful

Boxing remains one of Nepal’s most successful Asian Games disciplines, accounting for six bronze medals across three editions.

Nepal secured its maiden Asian Games medals at the 1986 Seoul Games, courtesy of Dal Bahadur Rana Magar, Tul Bahadur Thapa, Sushil Pokharel, and Manoj Bahadur Shrestha.

Chitra Bahadur Gurung added a bronze at the 1990 Beijing Games, while current national coach Deepak Maharjan won Nepal’s most recent boxing medal—a bronze at the 2010 Guangzhou Games. Nepal has been without an Asiad boxing medal since the 2014 Incheon Games.

Boxers feted

The squad was given an official send-off on Friday in a ceremony attended by NSC Member-Secretary Ram Charitra Mehta, NBA President Ram Awale, and other sports dignitaries.

During the event, the NBA also honoured four boxers with cash prizes and commendations for international achievements.

Chandra Bahadur Thapa: NRS 50,000 for his bronze medal performance (under-54 kg) at the 2025 IBA World Championships in Dubai.

Arpil Rana: NRS 20,000 for securing bronze (under-50 kg) at the 2025 Asian U-22 Boxing Championships in Thailand.

Lal Prasad Upreti & Anjani Teli: NRS 10,000 each in recognition of quarter-final finishes at the 2025 World Championships (under-51 kg) and the 2023 IBA Women’s World Boxing Championships (under-52 kg), respectively.

Separately, the Nepal Olympic Committee (NOC) hosted a farewell ceremony for the departing contingent at the NOC headquarters. NOC President Jeevan Ram Shrestha and Secretary General Rajiv Shrestha urged the athletes to maintain discipline and perform to their highest standards during the 40-day intensive training period in Guwahati ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.

भाग लेन॑ वाला टुकड़ी क॑ दू राजधानी स्थलऽ म॑ ठहरलऽ गेलऽ छै : सिनमंगल केरऽ रॉयल बुटीक होटल आरू गौशाला केरऽ पशुपति बुटीक होटल ।

रॉयल बुटीक होटल में जूडो, वुशु, महिला वॉलीबॉल, मुक्केबाजी, कराटे (काटा टीम), नृत्य खेल, साइकिलिंग, गोल्फ, एथलेटिक्स, आ तीरंदाजी के एथलीट आ कोचिंग स्टाफ के मेजबानी भ रहल अछि. एम्हर पशुपति बुटीक होटल में कराटे (कुमाइट टीम), ताइक्वांडो, सॉफ्ट टेनिस, टेनिस, तैराकी, स्क्वैश, बैडमिंटन, आ टेबल टेनिस के टीम के ठहरय के व्यवस्था अछि.वुशु, साइकिलिंग, गोल्फ, ताइक्वांडो, टेनिस, तैराकी, आ टेबल टेनिस के चुनल एथलीट एखन विदेश में प्रशिक्षण ल रहल छथि.

२०म एशियाई खेल १९ सितम्बर सँ ४ अक्टूबर धरि जापानक ऐची-नागोया मे चलत । नेपाल 22 विधा मे 136 एथलीट, 80 पुरुष आ 56 महिला कए मैदान मे उतारत।

भारत मे प्रशिक्षण लेत मुक्केबाजी दस्ता

खेल के तैयारी के तहत सात एथलीट सहित नौ सदस्यीय नेपाली मुक्केबाजी प्रतिनिधिमंडल भारत के खेल प्राधिकरण (एसएआई) के राष्ट्रीय उत्कृष्टता केंद्र में 40 दिन के गहन शिविर के लेल 10 अगस्त के असम के गुवाहाटी के लेल प्रस्थान करत।

नेपाल मुक्केबाजी संघक सचिव पुष्कर राज पन्त खेलसँ पहिने सीधा जापान दिस प्रस्थान धरि गुवाहाटीमे प्रशिक्षण लेत से पुष्टि केने छथि ।

टीम मे चारिटा पुरुष आ तीनटा महिला मुक्केबाज छथि।

पुरुष विभागमे चन्द्रबहादुर थापा (अंडर-५५ किलो), खगेन्द्र रोका मगर (अंडर-६० किलो), दान बहादुर दरलामी (अंडर-७० किलो), आ रबिन नेपाल (अंडर-९० किलो) अछि ।

महिला विभाग मे रमिषा श्रेष्ठ (अंडर-51 किलो), आस्मिता तामांग (अंडर-54 किलो), आ कुसुम तामांग (अंडर-65 किलो) छथि ।

रबिन नेपाल १९म एशियाई खेलसँ एकमात्र लौटनिहार दिग्गज छथि, जखन कि शेष ६ मुक्केबाज एशियामे डेब्यू करताह ।

टीम म॑ ऐतिहासिक पदक विजेता चंद्र बहादुर थापा न॑ शामिल छै, जेकरा न॑ दुबई म॑ आयोजित २०२५ केरऽ आईबीए विश्व मुक्केबाजी चैंपियनशिप म॑ पुरुषऽ के ५४ किलोग्राम स॑ कम वजन वर्ग म॑ कांस्य पदक हासिल करलकै, जे नेपाली मुक्केबाजी केरऽ इतिहास केरऽ सबस॑ उच्च अंतर्राष्ट्रीय उपलब्धि छेकै ।

कोच राज श्रेष्ठ आरू दीपक महर्जन प्रशिक्षण के देखरेख करतै, जेकरा म॑ एनबीए के महासचिव मन बहादुर भण्डारी टीम मैनेजर के रूप म॑ काम करतै ।

भण्डारी क॑ बाद म॑ भारत म॑ टीम म॑ शामिल होय के कार्यक्रम छै ।

मुक्केबाजी सबसे सफल

मुक्केबाजी नेपाल केरऽ सबसें सफल एशियाई खेलऽ के विधा म॑ स॑ एक बनलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ तीन संस्करणऽ म॑ छह कांस्य पदक मिललऽ छै ।

नेपाल १९८६ सियोल खेलमे दलबहादुर राणा मगर, तुल बहादुर थापा, सुशील पोखरेल, आ मनोज बहादुर श्रेष्ठके सौजन्यसँ पहिल बेर एशियन खेलमे पदक प्राप्त केलक ।

चित्र बहादुर गुरुंग न॑ १९९० केरऽ बीजिंग खेलऽ म॑ कांस्य पदक जोड़लकै, जबकि वर्तमान राष्ट्रीय कोच दीपक महर्जन न॑ नेपाल केरऽ सबसें ताजा मुक्केबाजी पदक जीतल॑ छेलै-२०१० केरऽ ग्वांगझू खेलऽ म॑ कांस्य पदक । नेपाल २०१४ इन्चियोन खेलके बाद एशियाड मुक्केबाजी पदकके बिना रहल अछि ।

मुक्केबाज भोज केलनि

शुक्रदिन एनएससी के सदस्य-सचिव राम चरित्र मेहता, एनबीए के अध्यक्ष राम आवाले, आओर अन्य खेल गणमान्य लोक के उपस्थिति मे टीम के आधिकारिक तौर पर भेजल गेल.

ई आयोजन के दौरान एनबीए न॑ चार मुक्केबाज क॑ नगद पुरस्कार आरू अंतरराष्ट्रीय उपलब्धि लेली प्रशंसा के साथ भी सम्मानित करलकै ।

चन्द्रबहादुर थापा : दुबईमे भेल २०२५ आईबीए विश्व चैम्पियनशिपमे कांस्य पदक प्रदर्शन (अंडर-५४ किलो) लेल एनआरएस ५० हजार ।

अर्पिल राना : थाईलैंड म॑ आयोजित २०२५ केरऽ एशियाई अंडर-२२ मुक्केबाजी चैंपियनशिप म॑ कांस्य पदक (अंडर-५० किलोग्राम) प्राप्त करै लेली २०,००० एनआरएस ।

लाल प्रसाद उप्रेती आरू अंजनी तेली : क्रमशः 2025 केरऽ विश्व चैंपियनशिप (51 किलोग्राम स॑ कम) आरू 2023 केरऽ आईबीए महिला विश्व मुक्केबाजी चैंपियनशिप (52 किलोग्राम स॑ कम) म॑ क्वार्टर फाइनल म॑ खतम होय के सम्मान म॑ एनआरएस 10,000-10,000 ।

अलग-अलग नेपाल ओलम्पिक समिति (एनओसी) द्वारा एनओसी मुख्यालय मे प्रस्थान करय वाला टुकड़ी के विदाई समारोह के आयोजन कायल गेल। एनओसी के अध्यक्ष जीवन राम श्रेष्ठ आरू महासचिव राजीव श्रेष्ठ न॑ ऐची-नागोया खेल स॑ पहल॑ गुवाहाटी म॑ ४० दिन के गहन प्रशिक्षण अवधि म॑ अनुशासन कायम रखै आरू उच्चतम स्तर के प्रदर्शन करै के आग्रह करलकै ।

title: Monsoon active across Nepal, heavy rain likely today - Khabarhub
description: Monsoon active across Nepal, heavy rain likely today  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Monsoon conditions remain active across Nepal, with the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology forecasting widespread cloud cover and rainfall in many parts of the country.

Heavy rain is likely in some hilly and mountainous areas, raising concerns over floods and landslides. The weather is generally cloudy in the Himalayan and hilly regions of the country, including Koshi, Madhes, and Bagmati provinces, while conditions are partly cloudy to mostly clear in the Terai.

Meanwhile, light rain accompanied by thunder is occurring in some places of Bagmati Province, while one or two places in Koshi, Madhes, and Lumbini provinces are also receiving light rainfall.

The Division has forecast generally cloudy weather across the country this afternoon. There is a possibility of moderate rain and snowfall in some mountainous areas of Koshi, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces.

Moderate rainfall is likely in many hilly areas of Koshi and Bagmati provinces and in some hilly areas of Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. Moderate rainfall is also expected in some parts of the Terai.

The Ddivision has warned of the possibility of heavy rainfall in one or two places in the mountainous and hilly areas of Koshi and Bagmati provinces.

Tonight, the weather is expected to remain generally cloudy throughout the country. Moderate rain and snowfall are likely in some mountainous and hilly regions.

Moderate rainfall is also expected in some Terai areas of Koshi, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, Madhes, and Sudurpaschim provinces, while one or two hilly areas of Karnali Province may receive heavy rainfall.

The Division has urged residents in vulnerable areas to take necessary precautions, as heavy rain may increase the risk of flash floods, floods, landslides, and soil erosion. It has also warned that the weather may affect daily life, agriculture, health services, tourism, mountaineering, and road and air transportation.

काठमाण्डु, मिथिला मिरर: नेपालमे मानसूनके अवस्था सक्रिय रहल अछि, जस तथा मौसम विज्ञान विभाग देशके अनेक भागमे व्यापक मेघ आवरण आ वर्षाके पूर्वानुमान लगा देने अछि ।

किछु पहाड़ी आ पहाड़ी इलाका मे भारी बरखा के संभावना अछि, जाहि सं बाढ़ि आओर भूस्खलन के चिंता बढ़ि रहल अछि. कोशी, मधेश, आरू बागमती प्रांत सहित देश केरऽ हिमालय आरू पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ मौसम सामान्यतः बादल वाला होय छै, जबकि तराई म॑ हालात आंशिक रूप स॑ बादल वाला स॑ अधिकतर साफ होय छै ।

अहिना, बागमती प्रदेशके किछ ठाममे गरजके साथ हल्के वर्षा भऽ रहल अछि, तहिना कोशी, मधेश, आ लुम्बिनी प्रदेशमे एक-दू ठाममे सेहो हल्के वर्षा भऽ रहल अछि ।

डिवीजन न॑ आय दुपहर म॑ देश भर म॑ सामान्य तौर प॑ बादल छाए वाला मौसम के पूर्वानुमान लगैलकै । कोशी, बागमती, गण्डकी, लुम्बिनी, कर्णाली, आ सुदुरपश्चिम प्रांतक किछु पहाड़ी क्षेत्र मे मध्यम वर्षा आ बर्फबारी के संभावना अछि ।

कोशी आरू बागमती प्रांत केरऽ बहुत पहाड़ी क्षेत्र आरू गंडकी, लुम्बिनी, कर्णाली, आरू सुदुरपश्चिम प्रांत केरऽ कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ मध्यम वर्षा के संभावना छै । तराई के किछ इलाका मे मध्यम वर्षा के सेहो संभावना अछि.

कोशी आ बागमती प्रांत के पहाड़ी आ पहाड़ी इलाका मे एक-दू ठाम भारी बरखा के संभावना के बारे मे डीडिवीजन चेतावनी देलक अछि।

आइ राति देश भरि मे मौसम सामान्यतः बादल छाएत रहबाक संभावना अछि। किछु पहाड़ी आ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र मे मध्यम वर्षा आ बर्फबारी के संभावना अछि ।

कोशी, बागमती, गण्डकी, लुम्बिनी, मधेश, आ सुदुरपश्चिम प्रदेशके किछु तराई क्षेत्रमे सेहो मध्यम वर्षाके सम्भावना अछि, जखन कि कर्णाली प्रदेशके एक-दू पहाड़ी क्षेत्रमे भारी वर्षा भऽ सकैत अछि ।

डिवीजन न॑ कमजोर क्षेत्रऽ के निवासी स॑ आग्रह करल॑ छै कि हुनी आवश्यक सावधानी बरतै, कैन्हेंकि भारी बारिश के कारण आकस्मिक बाढ़, बाढ़, भूस्खलन, आरू माटी के कटाव के खतरा बढ़ी सकै छै । एकरा म॑ ई भी चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छै कि मौसम केरऽ असर दैनिक जीवन, कृषि, स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पर्यटन, पर्वतारोहण, आरू सड़क आरू हवाई परिवहन प॑ पड़॑ सकै छै ।

title: Nepal rolls out insurance against wildlife attacks - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal rolls out insurance against wildlife attacks  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
When Dhurbe, the notorious elephant, emerged from the forest in Jagatpur last month, few villagers could have predicted who would cross his path next.

The adult male tusker charged into a settlement bordering Chitwan National Park and killed Ashika Bote and her young son, adding two more names to a grim record that stretches back more than a decade. According to wildlife officials, Dhurbe has been responsible for 25 human deaths since 2010, and is one of Nepal’s deadliest wild animals. For Ashika’s family, the loss reopened an old wound: Dhurbe had already claimed the lives of two relatives in Madi in 2012.

Their deaths have renewed attention to a growing crisis across Nepal’s forest fringes. As wildlife populations recover and human settlements continue to expand along the edges of protected areas, encounters between people and wild animals are becoming more frequent— and often deadly.

The Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation recorded more than 9,900 cases of wildlife attacks on people in its 2024-25 annual report. Nineteen people were killed, 53 suffered serious injuries, and another 50 sustained minor injuries. Chitwan National Park, Nepal’s flagship conservation area, has recorded more than 120 human deaths from wildlife attacks over the past decade.

In Bardiya district, wildlife killed 11 people between mid-July last year and June this year, nearly doubling the previous year’s death toll. Leopards accounted for eight of those deaths, while tigers killed two people and an elephant killed another. Fifteen others were injured during the same period, after which a joint team from the Division Forest Office, Bardiya National Park, and the National Trust for Nature Conservation captured six leopards identified as posing repeated threats to nearby communities. Even so, residents in municipalities including Gulariya, Rajapur, Madhuwan, and Bardiya continue to report leopard incursions into settlements.

Across Nepal, wild animals have killed 146 people over the past five years. Another 399 people suffered serious injuries and 251 sustained minor injuries. Elephants, rhinos, tigers, leopards, bears, wild dogs, and crocodiles have also destroyed homes, livestock sheds, standing crops, and caused heavy financial losses on households that depend on farming for their livelihoods. During the same period, the government spent nearly Rs586 million compensating victims of wildlife-related incidents.

For decades, Nepal’s primary response has been to compensate victims after attacks occur. Families could apply for government relief for deaths, injuries, damaged houses, livestock losses, and destroyed crops, but the process depended on official verification and government disbursement.

Last month, Nepal introduced a different approach.

Beginning July 17, non-life insurance companies licensed by the Nepal Insurance Authority began offering the country’s first Wildlife Risk Insurance Policy. Developed in response to requests from provincial and local governments, conservation authorities and communities living in wildlife-prone areas, the scheme is intended to complement the existing government relief system rather than replace it.

For an annual premium of Rs1,500, households can purchase protection against death, injury, and property losses caused by attacks by 18 species of wild animals, including elephants, tigers, rhinoceroses, leopards, bears, and crocodiles. Coverage includes up to Rs1 million for accidental death or permanent disability, Rs 500,000 for temporary disability, Rs 100,000 for treatment of serious injuries, and Rs 20,000 for minor injuries. The policy also insures houses, livestock, and agricultural crops, while providing Rs50,000 within seven days to help families cover funeral expenses after a fatal attack.

The policy marks Nepal’s first attempt to manage wildlife risk through insurance. Officials hope it will provide households with faster financial support after attacks while easing pressure on government compensation programmes. Whether it succeeds will depend not only on how widely communities adopt it, but also on whether it can reduce the economic insecurity that often follows living alongside wildlife.

Binod Kumar Pokharel, deputy director at the Nepal Insurance Authority, said the scheme was designed as a pilot and could be refined as insurers begin issuing policies and processing claims.

“This wildlife policy has been formulated on the request of provincial and local governments, especially Koshi Province, Mechi Municipality, and the Department of National Parks,” Pokharel said.

Because Nepal had no previous wildlife insurance programme to use as a model, the insurance authority looked to existing insurance products when determining the Rs1,500 premium, he said. The coverage limits were also designed to ensure victims would receive at least as much support as they currently receive through government relief programmes.

“NIA has taken this product as a pilot product for this year and will revise it accordingly in the following year,” he said. “The major expectation is that this policy will reduce the financial and administrative burden of the government in the days to come.”

The insurance policy will operate alongside, rather than replace, the government's existing Wildlife Damage Relief Distribution Guidelines.

Under the current relief system, families of people killed by wildlife can receive up to Rs1 million from the government. Serious injuries are compensated up to Rs200,000, permanent disability up to Rs500,000, and minor injuries up to Rs20,000. Relief is also available for livestock, damaged houses, grain stores, and seasonal crops, although the payment ceilings are generally lower than the insurance coverage now being offered.

Relief payments, however, depend on official verification and government disbursement. Victims or their families must report incidents, obtain recommendations from local authorities, and submit supporting medical or veterinary records before claims are approved. While the revised 2080 (Bikram Sambat), Nepali year guidelines simplified the process by allowing applications to be filed at nearby forest offices, payments still depend on administrative procedures and the availability of government funds.

The insurance scheme is intended to provide an additional layer of financial protection. Whether the policy will reduce conflict between people and wildlife, however, remains an open question.

Conservation scientists say the policy could ease some of the financial hardship that fuels resentment towards wildlife, but stress that compensation alone cannot prevent attacks or address the factors driving conflict.

Prakash Kumar Paudel, a conservation scientist who researches human-wildlife conflict, said the policy should be understood as one component of a much broader strategy for coexistence.

“Coexistence means both reducing people's exposure to wildlife and improving their resilience when conflict occurs,” Paudel said. “Human-wildlife conflict involves social, economic, and ecological dynamics that are all interconnected. Insurance is one instrument that can reduce economic vulnerability by compensating for losses caused by wildlife.”

He said insurance could help soften negative attitudes towards wildlife by reducing the financial shock experienced by affected households, particularly those that lose crops or livestock.

Paudel said the policy’s comprehensive coverage and provision for faster payments were encouraging, but cautioned that its success would depend on implementation.

“If this policy is implemented alongside education, awareness programmes and other support systems, it can help reduce the negative perceptions that often arise after wildlife attacks,” he said. “But it does not directly address the underlying causes of conflict.”

Babu Ram Lamichhane, a conservation biologist who has studied human-wildlife conflict in Nepal, said growing losses have eroded support for wildlife conservation in many buffer-zone communities.

“There is a growing concern from local communities regarding losses caused by wildlife,” Lamichhane said. “Many people are increasingly becoming negative towards wildlife because of these losses. From a conservation perspective, this policy is an excellent initiative because it can reduce that financial burden and support coexistence.”

Still, Lamichhane said it remains to be seen whether the programme will prove financially sustainable if claims become frequent in areas with high rates of human casualties.

“If the policy is widely accepted and adopted, it has the potential to address one of the biggest frustrations communities face, which is compensation for wildlife damage,” he said. “But we will only know how effective it is once we see how both communities and insurance companies respond in practice.”

Both scientists emphasised that insurance should complement, not replace, efforts to prevent conflict in the first place.

“Insurance should never be treated as a complete solution to human-wildlife conflict,” Paudel said. “We also need stronger conflict-mitigation measures such as barriers, changes in cropping patterns, habitat improvement inside forests and protected areas, conservation awareness and behaviour change.”

Lamichhane agreed, saying preventive measures should remain the priority.

“Reducing losses through prevention should always come first,” he said. “Physical barriers, early warning systems, cultivation of crops that wildlife are less likely to eat, and awareness programmes all remain essential. Insurance and government relief are important because they help reduce resentment and the risk of retaliation against wildlife, but they cannot replace prevention.”

The policy may also have implications beyond conservation.

Rakesh Gyawali, a sustainable finance professional, believes the policy expands the role insurance can play in Nepal’s approach to climate and environmental risks.

Discussions about sustainable finance often centre on green investment, climate funds, and environmental, social, and governance standards, he said. Risk management receives much less attention, even though it influences whether households and businesses are willing to invest.

“By providing financial protection against wildlife-related losses, it has the potential to reduce uncertainty for people and businesses operating in wildlife-prone areas,” Gyawali said. “Insurance complements financing by helping strengthen resilience alongside investment and economic activity.”

He said many households and small businesses in buffer-zone communities hesitate to invest in agriculture, agroforestry, ecotourism and other nature-based enterprises because a single wildlife attack can wipe out years of savings. Insurance cannot eliminate those risks, Gyawali said, but it can help families recover more quickly, protect productive assets, and continue their livelihoods after losses.

As Nepal grapples with growing human-wildlife conflict, the policy represents a shift in thinking — from simply compensating losses after tragedy to building the financial resilience of communities living alongside wildlife.

पिछला मास जखन जगतपुर क जंगल स कुख्यात हाथी धुरबे निकलल छल त अगिला बेर ओकर बाट के पार करत, एकर अंदाजा कम गामक लोक क सकैत छल।

वयस्क नर टस्कर न॑ चितवन नेशनल पार्क के सीमा प॑ बनलऽ एगो बस्ती म॑ हमला करी क॑ आशिका बोटे आरू ओकरऽ छोटऽ बेटा क॑ मारलकै, जेकरा स॑ एक दशक स॑ भी अधिक समय केरऽ भयावह रिकॉर्ड म॑ दू नाम आरू जोड़लऽ गेलै । वन्यजीव अधिकारी के अनुसार धुरबे 2010 स॑ 25 मानव मौत के जिम्मेदार छै, आरू नेपाल केरऽ सबसें घातक जंगली जानवरऽ म॑ स॑ एक छै । आशिका’क परिवार’क लेल ई नुकसान एकटा पुरान घाव केँ फेर सँ खोललक: धुरबे 2012 मे मादी मे दू टा रिश्तेदार’क जान ल’ चुकल छल.

हुनकऽ मौत स॑ नेपाल केरऽ जंगल केरऽ किनारे बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ संकट प॑ ध्यान नया रूप देलऽ गेलऽ छै । जेना-जेना वन्यजीवक कें आबादी ठीक भ रहल छै आ संरक्षित क्षेत्रक कें किनारक पर मानव बस्तीक कें विस्तार जारी छै, लोगक आ जंगली जानवरक कें बीच मुठभेड़ बेसि भ रहल छै- आ अक्सर घातक भ रहल छै.

राष्ट्रीय उद्यान आरू वन्यजीव संरक्षण विभाग न॑ अपनऽ २०२४-२५ केरऽ वार्षिक रिपोर्ट म॑ लोगऽ प॑ वन्यजीव हमला के ९,९०० स॑ भी अधिक मामला दर्ज करलकै । 19 गोटेक मौत भेल, 53 गोटे गंभीर रूप सं घायल भेलाह, आओर 50 गोटे के मामूली चोट लागल अछि. नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख संरक्षण क्षेत्र चितवन राष्ट्रिय उद्यान म॑ पिछला एक दशक म॑ वन्यजीव केरऽ हमला स॑ १२० स॑ भी अधिक मानव मृत्यु दर्ज करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

बर्दिया जिला में पिछला साल जुलाई के मध्य सं एहि साल जून के बीच वन्यजीव के कारण 11 लोक के मौत भ गेल छल, जे पिछला साल के मौत के संख्या सं लगभग दुगुना भ गेल अछि. ओहि मे सं आठ गोटेक मौत तेंदुआ के भेल, जखन कि बाघ दू गोटे के मारि देलक आ एकटा हाथी एकटा आओर के मारि देलक. यही दौरान पन्द्रह अन्य लोग घायल होय गेलै, जेकरा बाद डिवीजन वन कार्यालय, बर्दिया नेशनल पार्क, आरू नेशनल ट्रस्ट फॉर नेचर कंजरवेशन के संयुक्त टीम न॑ छह तेंदुआ क॑ पकड़ी लेलकै, जेकरा पास के समुदाय लेली बार-बार खतरा पैदा करै वाला के रूप म॑ पहचानलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । तइयो गुलारिया, राजापुर, मधुवान, आ बर्दिया सहित नगरपालिकाक निवासी बस्ती मे तेंदुआक आक्रमणक सूचना दैत रहैत छथि ।

सम्पूर्ण नेपालमे विगत ५ वर्षमे १४६ गोटेके जंगली जानवरके मृत्यु भेल अछि । आर 399 गोटे गंभीर रूप सं घायल आ 251 गोटे के मामूली चोट लागल अछि। हाथी, गैंडा, बाघ, तेंदुआ, भालू, जंगली कुकुर, आरू मगरमच्छ भी घरऽ, पशुपालन केरऽ शेड, खड़ा फसल क॑ तबाह करी देल॑ छै, आरू रोजी-रोटी लेली खेती प॑ निर्भर घरऽ क॑ भारी आर्थिक नुकसान पहुँचैलकै । एहि दौरान सरकार वन्यजीव सं जुड़ल घटना के शिकार लोक के मुआवजा मे करीब 58.6 करोड़ रुपया खर्च केलक।

दशकों स नेपाल के प्राथमिक प्रतिक्रिया हमला के बाद पीड़ित के मुआवजा देबय के अछि. परिवार मौत, चोट, क्षतिग्रस्त घर, पशुधन के नुकसान, आ नष्ट फसल के लेल सरकारी राहत के लेल आवेदन क सकैत छल, मुदा ई प्रक्रिया आधिकारिक सत्यापन आ सरकारी वितरण पर निर्भर करैत छल.

पिछला मास नेपाल एकटा अलग तरीका शुरू केलक।

17 जुलाई सं नेपाल बीमा प्राधिकरण सं लाइसेंस प्राप्त गैर-जीवन बीमा कंपनी देशक पहिल वन्यजीव जोखिम बीमा पॉलिसी देबय लागल. प्रांतीय आ स्थानीय सरकारक, संरक्षण प्राधिकारीक आ वन्यजीव प्रवण क्षेत्रक मे रहय वाला समुदायक कें अनुरोधक कें जवाब मे विकसित कैल गेल इ योजना कें उद्देश्य मौजूदा सरकारी राहत प्रणाली कें बदलय कें बजाय ओकर पूरक बनानाय छै.

1500 रुपया कें वार्षिक प्रीमियम पर घरक हाथी, बाघ, गैंडा, तेंदुआ, भालू, आ मगरमच्छ सहित 18 प्रजातियक कें जंगली जानवरक कें हमला सं मौत, चोट, आ संपत्ति कें नुकसान सं सुरक्षा खरीद सकय छै. कवरेज मे आकस्मिक मृत्यु या स्थायी विकलांगता कें लेल 10 लाख रुपया तइक, अस्थायी विकलांगता कें लेल 5 लाख रुपया, गंभीर चोट कें इलाज कें लेल एक लाख रुपया, आ मामूली चोट कें लेल 20 हजार रुपया शामिल छै. एहि पॉलिसी मे घर, पशुधन, आ कृषि फसल क बीमा सेहो कैल गेल अछि, जखन कि सात दिन क भीतर 50 हजार टका क प्रावधान कैल गेल अछि, जाहि स परिवार कए जानलेवा हमला क बाद अंतिम संस्कार क खर्च पूरा करबा मे मदद भेटत।

ई पॉलिसी नेपाल केरऽ पहिलऽ प्रयास छै कि बीमा के माध्यम स॑ वन्यजीव केरऽ जोखिम के प्रबंधन करलऽ जाय । अधिकारी कए उम्मीद अछि जे एहि स हमला क बाद घर कए तेजी स आर्थिक मदद भेटत आ संगहि सरकारी मुआवजा कार्यक्रम पर दबाव कम भ जाएत। ई सफल होय या नै, ई न सिर्फ ई बात प॑ निर्भर करतै कि समुदाय एकरा कतेक व्यापक रूप स॑ अपनाबै छै, बल्कि ई बात प॑ भी निर्भर करतै कि ई आर्थिक असुरक्षा क॑ कम करी सकै छै कि अक्सर वन्यजीवऽ के साथ-साथ रहला के बाद पैदा होय छै ।

नेपाल बीमा प्राधिकरणके उपनिदेशक बिनोद कुमार पोखरेल कहलनि जे, योजना के पायलट के रूप में डिजाइन कएल गेल अछि आ बीमा कंपनी पॉलिसी जारी करय आ दावा के प्रक्रिया शुरू करय के कारण एकरा परिष्कृत कएल जा सकैत अछि।

पोखरेल कहलनि जे, ई वन्यजीव नीति प्रांतीय आ स्थानीय सरकार खास क कोशी प्रांत, मेची नगरपालिका, आ राष्ट्रीय उद्यान विभाग के आग्रह पर बनायल गेल अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे मॉडल के रूप मे उपयोग करय लेल पहिने वन्यजीव बीमा कार्यक्रम नहि छल, ताहि लेल बीमा प्राधिकरण 1500 रुपया के प्रीमियम निर्धारित करय काल मौजूदा बीमा उत्पाद के देखैत छल। कवरेज सीमा इ सुनिश्चित करय कें लेल सेहो बनायल गेल छल जे पीड़ितक कें कम सं कम ओतबे सहयोग मिलत जतेक कि ओकरा वर्तमान मे सरकारी राहत कार्यक्रमक कें माध्यम सं भेटय छै.

ओ कहला जे एनआईए एहि साल क लेल एहि उत्पाद कए पायलट उत्पाद क रूप मे लेलक अछि आ अगिला साल एहि हिसाब स एकरा संशोधित करत। “बड़का उम्मीद अछि जे एहि नीति स आबै वाला दिन मे सरकार क आर्थिक आ प्रशासनिक बोझ कम भ जाएत।”

बीमा पॉलिसी सरकार कें मौजूदा वन्यजीव क्षति राहत वितरण दिशा निर्देशक कें बदलय कें बजाय, साथ-साथ संचालित होयत.

वर्तमान राहत प्रणाली के तहत वन्यजीव द्वारा मारल गेल लोक के परिवार के सरकार सं 10 लाख रुपया तक के राशि भेट सकैत अछि. गंभीर चोट के दू लाख रुपया तक, स्थायी विकलांगता के पांच लाख रुपया तक, आ मामूली चोट के 20 हजार रुपया तक के मुआवजा देल गेल अछि। पशुधन, क्षतिग्रस्त घर, अनाज कें भंडार, आ मौसमी फसलक कें लेल सेहो राहत उपलब्ध छै, हालांकि भुगतान कें सीमा आमतौर पर आब देल जा रहल बीमा कवरेज सं कम छै.

राहत कें भुगतान, तथापि, आधिकारिक सत्यापन आ सरकारी वितरण पर निर्भर करय छै. पीड़ित या ओकर परिवार कें दावा कें मंजूरी सं पहिले घटनाक कें रिपोर्ट करनाय, स्थानीय प्राधिकारीक सं सिफारिशक लेनाय, आ सहायक चिकित्सा या पशु चिकित्सा रिकॉर्ड जमा करनाय आवश्यक छै. संशोधित २०८० (बिक्रम सम्बत), नेपाली वर्ष दिशानिर्देश मे जखन कि नजदीकी वन कार्यालय मे आवेदन दाखिल करबाक अनुमति दऽ प्रक्रिया केँ सरल बना देल गेल, मुदा भुगतान एखनो प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया आ सरकारी धनक उपलब्धता पर निर्भर करैत अछि ।

बीमा योजना कें उद्देश्य आर्थिक सुरक्षा कें एकटा अतिरिक्त परत प्रदान करनाय छै. लेकिन ई नीति स॑ लोगऽ आरू वन्यजीव के बीच टकराव म॑ कमी ​​आबै वाला छै कि नै, ई एगो खुला सवाल बनलऽ छै ।

संरक्षण वैज्ञानिकऽ के कहना छै कि ई नीति वन्यजीव के प्रति आक्रोश पैदा करै वाला कुछ आर्थिक कठिनाई क॑ कम करी सकै छै, लेकिन ई बात प॑ जोर दै छै कि केवल मुआवजा हमला क॑ रोकी नै सकै छै आरू नै ही टकराव क॑ बढ़ाबै वाला कारक क॑ संबोधित नै करी सकै छै ।

मानव-वन्यजीव संघर्ष के शोध करै वाला संरक्षण वैज्ञानिक प्रकाश कुमार पौडेल नँ कहलकै कि ई नीति क सह-अस्तित्व के बहुत व्यापक रणनीति के एक घटक के रूप मँ समझलौ जाना चाहिय्यौ ।

पौडेल नँ कहलकै, “सह-अस्तित्व के मतलब छै कि लोगऽ के वन्यजीव के संपर्क म॑ आबै म॑ कमी ​​आरू संघर्ष घटला प॑ ओकरऽ लचीलापन म॑ सुधार दूनू छै । "मानव-वन्यजीव संघर्ष म॑ सामाजिक, आर्थिक, आरू पारिस्थितिकी गतिशीलता शामिल छै जे सब एक दोसरा स॑ जुड़लऽ छै ।बीमा एगो ऐन्हऽ साधन छै जे वन्यजीवऽ स॑ होय वाला नुकसान के भरपाई करी क॑ आर्थिक कमजोरी क॑ कम करी सकै छै।"

हुनी कहलकै कि बीमा प्रभावित घरौ खास करी क फसल या पशुधन के नुकसान करै वाला घरौ क आर्थिक झटका क कम करी क वन्यजीव के प्रति नकारात्मक दृष्टिकोण क नरम करै मँ मदद करी सकै छै ।

पौडेल न॑ कहलकै कि नीति केरऽ व्यापक कवरेज आरू तेजी स॑ भुगतान के प्रावधान उत्साहजनक छै, लेकिन चेतावनी देलकै कि एकरऽ सफलता लागू करै प॑ निर्भर करतै ।

हुनी कहलकै, “जदि ई नीति क॑ शिक्षा, जागरूकता कार्यक्रम आरू अन्य सहायता प्रणाली के साथ-साथ लागू करलऽ जाय त॑ ई वन्यजीवऽ के हमला के बाद अक्सर पैदा होय वाला नकारात्मक धारणा क॑ कम करै म॑ मदद करी सकै छै । “मुदा ई सीधा-सीधा द्वंद्व के अंतर्निहित कारण के संबोधित नै करै छै।”

नेपाल मे मानव-वन्यजीव द्वंद्वक अध्ययन केनिहार संरक्षण जीवविज्ञानी बाबू राम लामिछाने कहलनि जे, बढ़ैत नुकसान के कारण बफर जोन के बहुतो समुदाय मे वन्यजीव संरक्षण के समर्थन क्षीण भ गेल अछि।

लामिछाने कहला जे वन्यजीव स होए वाला नुकसान क संबंध मे स्थानीय समुदाय क चिंता बढ़ि रहल अछि। "ई नुकसान के कारण बहुत लोग वन्यजीव के प्रति नकारात्मक होय रहलऽ छै । संरक्षण के दृष्टिकोण स॑ ई नीति एगो बेहतरीन पहल छै, कैन्हेंकि ई वू आर्थिक बोझ क॑ कम करी सकै छै आरू सह-अस्तित्व के समर्थन करी सकै छै।"

तइयो लामिछाने नँ कहलकै कि ई देखना छै कि अगर मानव हताहत के अधिक दर वाला इलाका मँ दावा बार-बार होय जाय छै त ई कार्यक्रम आर्थिक रूप सँ टिकाऊ साबित होतै कि नै ।

हुनी कहलकै, “जदि ई नीति क व्यापक रूप स॑ स्वीकार करी क॑ अपनालऽ जाय छै त॑ एकरा म॑ समुदायऽ क॑ सामने आबै वाला सबस॑ बड़ऽ कुंठा म॑ स॑ एगो क॑ संबोधित करै के क्षमता छै, जे वन्यजीवऽ के नुकसान के मुआवजा छै । “मुदा ई कतेक प्रभावी अछि तखने पता चलत जखन हम देखब जे समुदाय आ बीमा कंपनी दुनू व्यवहार मे केहन प्रतिक्रिया दैत अछि।”

दुनू वैज्ञानिक एहि बात पर जोर देलनि जे बीमा पहिल बेर टकराव रोकबाक प्रयास के पूरक हेबाक चाही, ओकर जगह नहि लेबाक चाही.

पौडेल कहला जे बीमा कए कहियो मानव-वन्यजीव टकराव क पूर्ण समाधान नहि मानल जेबाक चाही। “हमरा सब क॑ संघर्ष-शमन केरऽ मजबूत उपाय भी चाही जेना कि बाधा, फसल के पैटर्न म॑ बदलाव, जंगल आरू संरक्षित क्षेत्रऽ के भीतर आवास म॑ सुधार, संरक्षण जागरूकता आरू व्यवहार म॑ बदलाव।”

लामिछाने एहि बात पर सहमत होइत कहलनि जे निवारक उपाय प्राथमिकता बनल रहबाक चाही।

ओ कहला जे रोकथाम क माध्यम स नुकसान कम करब सदिखन सबस पहिने रहबाक चाही। “भौतिक बाधा, जल्दी चेतावनी प्रणाली, फसल के खेती जेकरा वन्यजीव खाबै के संभावना कम छै, आरू जागरूकता कार्यक्रम सब जरूरी छै । बीमा आ सरकारी राहत महत्वपूर्ण छै, कियाकि इ आक्रोश आ वन्यजीवक कें खिलाफ जवाबी कार्रवाई कें जोखिम कें कम करय मे मदद करय छै, मुदा इ रोकथाम कें जगह नहि ल सकय छै.”

एहि नीति क संरक्षण स आगू सेहो निहितार्थ भ सकैत अछि।

टिकाऊ वित्त पेशेवर राकेश ग्यावाली के मानना छै कि ई पॉलिसी जलवायु आरू पर्यावरणीय जोखिम के प्रति नेपाल के दृष्टिकोण म॑ बीमा के भूमिका के विस्तार करै छै ।

हुनी कहलकै कि टिकाऊ वित्त के बारे मँ चर्चा अक्सर हरित निवेश, जलवायु कोष, आरू पर्यावरण, सामाजिक, आरू शासन मानक प केंद्रित छै । जोखिम प्रबंधन पर बहुत कम ध्यान देल जायत छै, भले ही इ प्रभावित करयत छै की घर आ व्यवसाय निवेश करय कें लेल तैयार छै या नहि.

ज्ञानवाली नँ कहलकै, “वन्यजीव सँ जुड़लौ नुकसान के खिलाफ आर्थिक सुरक्षा प्रदान करी क वन्यजीव प्रवण क्षेत्र मँ संचालित लोग आरू व्यवसाय लेली अनिश्चितता क कम करै के क्षमता छै । “बीमा निवेश आरू आर्थिक गतिविधि के साथ-साथ लचीलापन क॑ मजबूत करै म॑ मदद करी क॑ वित्तपोषण के पूरक छै।”

हुनी कहलकै कि बफर-जोन समुदाय मँ बहुत सारा घर आरू छोटौ व्यवसाय कृषि, कृषि वानिकी, इकोटूरिज्म आरू अन्य प्रकृति आधारित उद्यम मँ निवेश करै मँ संकोच करै छै, कैन्हेंकि वन्यजीव के एक हमला स॑ सालौ के बचत के समाप्त होय सकै छै । ज्ञानवाली न॑ कहलकै कि बीमा वू जोखिम क॑ खतम नै करी सकै छै, लेकिन ई परिवारऽ क॑ जल्दी स॑ ठीक होय म॑ मदद करी सकै छै, उत्पादक संपत्ति के सुरक्षा करी सकै छै, आरू नुकसान के बाद ओकरऽ रोजी-रोटी जारी रखै म॑ मदद करी सकै छै ।

जेना-जेना नेपाल बढ़ैत मानव-वन्यजीव संघर्ष स॑ जूझै छै, ई नीति सोच म॑ बदलाव के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै — खाली त्रासदी के बाद नुकसान के भरपाई करै स॑ ल॑ क॑ वन्यजीव के साथ-साथ रह॑ वाला समुदायऽ के आर्थिक लचीलापन के निर्माण तक ।
